articles.title: More Programs or More Rolls? Separating Coverage from Specialization in LLM Harnesses
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.35873v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated generation of LLM harnesses promises to improve inference through task specialization. Yet additional answer coverage can arise from repeated execution of the same program, making specialization difficult to identify. articles.title: PowerZooJax: A JAX-based Power System Benchmark for Reinforcement Learning
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.36052v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Power system operation is a safety-critical sequential decision-making problem, making it a natural testbed for reinforcement learning (RL). However, existing RL environments for power systems are often narrow in scope and computationally limited by CPU-based simulation workflows, making large-scale evaluation difficult. articles.title: Is Human-Readable Text Necessary for Effective LLM Fine-Tuning?
articles.description:
arXiv:2609.35868v1 Announce Type: new

articles.title: SAGE: A Statistical Acceptance Gate for Self-Evolving Agents
articles.description:
